messages:
Lina (SE): Quick sync — AcmeBank POC in 24h. They need streaming SDK + function/tool calls that emit strict JSON (schema-validated) per record, plus answers for pricing and SOC2. Can eng confirm end-to-end feasibility and any POC blockers?
Marco (DevEx): We support streaming via SSE and WebSocket in our Go/Node/Rust SDKs. Function/tool calls are supported in-stream; they return structured JSON that matches declared schemas. Will paste minimal snippets and guidance below.
Sam (Sales): Customer expects ~100k tokens/day during POC with bursts. They asked if we can do a 1-month reserved for predictable latency — what do we recommend for pricing/math?
Anya (Customer Eng): From security side: they want SOC2 report, IP allowlist, and ephemeral creds for the POC. We can provide SOC2 and short-lived creds (STS) + IP allowlist for hosted; if they want VPC/private we need a ticket for Private deployment.
Marco (DevEx): Code snippet for SSE streaming + function calls (Go SDK):
```
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey)
stream := client.Stream(ctx, modelOpt.WithStreaming())
stream.OnEvent(func(ev Event) {
  switch ev.Type {
  case EventToolCall:
    // payload is JSON matching declared schema
    handleToolCall(ev.Payload)
  case EventPartial:
    // partial generation chunk
  }
})
stream.Send(prompt)
```
Marco (DevEx): Important: declare function schema in the request. The runtime will validate outputs against schema and emit a final `tool_result` event with the validated JSON. During streaming you get incremental chunks plus `tool_call`/`tool_result` events — handle accordingly.
Lina (SE): For the POC we need a tiny sample that shows: 1) streaming function call that returns array-of-records JSON, 2) how to resume after reconnect, 3) metrics to capture (latency/token cost). Marco can you add the resume handshake notes?
Marco (DevEx): Resume/handshake: include `x-redwood-session` header with session id. If connection drops, client reopens with last-ack sequence; server will replay cached KV up to sequence and continue. For best cost, enable prefix KV caching on model config.
Sam (Sales): Pricing: can we offer a short-term reserved (1 month) with a small commit and burst credits? What tier maps to 100k tokens/day?
Anya (Customer Eng): Suggest reserved-sml tier for POC (committed 0.5 GPU-equivalent), we can add 2x burst buffer for spikes. I'll loop in finance for a POC quote.
Marco (DevEx): Note on structured output: if you need strict schemas for arrays of objects, use `response_format: {type: "array", items: {type: "object", properties: {...}}}`. The runtime enforces and will surface schema violations as `tool_result.error`. For streaming consumers, treat `tool_result` as the canonical single JSON — partial chunks are not guaranteed valid JSON until final.
Lina (SE): Any enterprise blockers? latency or auth gaps?
Anya (Customer Eng): Two potential blockers: 1) Customer SSO + SAML — for hosted POC we need SAML workaround or invite-only accounts; 2) Legal wants subprocessor list before signing exchange. Both are standard, will track.
Sam (Sales): I'll ask them to accept invite accounts for the POC and send the subprocessor doc. Can we produce a one-pager with steps for SDK hookup + sample payloads for their infra team?
Marco (DevEx): I can draft a one-pager and a runnable example repo tonight. Will include Node/Go snippets, resume handshake, event list (tool_call, tool_chunk, tool_result), and the minimal model/config settings (batching off for low latency, kv_prefix_cache enabled).
Lina (SE): Awesome. Also add a note about observability: route-level token breakdown + per-request latency traces — helps them validate SLA.
deploy-bot: Canary for acme-poc-sample created: canary-20240315-34 (link: https://console.redwood/acme/canary).
Sam (Sales): :thumbsup: Thanks everyone — I'll bundle answers for the customer and request the POC commit once we have the quote and one-pager.
Marco (DevEx): Leaving a small gotcha: if they plan to post-process tool_result on their side, ensure they call `validate_schema` with our SDK helper to avoid silent schema drift.
Lina (SE): Perfect. Closing loop: Marco -> one-pager + sample repo, Anya -> SOC2 + subprocessor, Finance -> POC quote. Ping here when ready. :wave:
